Rhombus Sand Station is a station on Neko Line. It is operated by Phantasia Metro, and is located at Los Sengas Yowah. Passengers may also use this station to change to Element Hub Transit Hook Sand Line (Rhombus Sand Station), Arcgo City Railway Prosand Corridor (Rhombus Sand Station) and Central-Yowah Railway Yowah Line, Yowah Line (Rapid) (Rhombus Sand Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • There is no direct access from the concourse to the exits of this station. Instead, a Exit Passageway system similar to that of Enning Station is adopted at this station.

History[]

  • February 6 2023: This Station began construction.[2]
  • February 12 2023: This Station completed construction.[3]
  • February 13 2023: Urban Line trains began stopping at this station, but Aquilo Circuit Platforms remain reserved.
  • April 7 2025: This Station completed setting up of Aquilo Circuit systems.[4]
  • April 22 2025: Aquilo Circuit is established.

Rice Lake EHT Station Stop is a station of SLT Line 2610L. It is located at Los Sengas Prymea. Passengers may also use this station to change to Element Hub Transit Evillow Line (Rice Lake Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • This station shares structure with Rice Lake EHT Station Stop. However, as Rice Lake University is currently under construction, access to that Station was sealed off prior to the opening of SLT Line 2610L.
  • The Concourse of this station adopts a crowd control pattern in anticipation of future passenger flow.
  • Before this station was constructed, the location of this station was mistakenly assumed as the location of Spring Point Gateway, and the village nearby this station was hence named "Spring Point Village".
  • The station number of Evillow Line for this station was EV-12. However, it has later been changed to EV-14 due to Station Number rearrangements.

River Rendezvous Station is a station on Egress Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Egress. Passengers may also use this station to change to Haisan Railway Peninsula Line (River Rendezvous Station) and SLT Line 2002 (River Rendezvous Stop).

Fun Facts[]

  • Rendezvous is a word of French origin that refers to a place designated for a meeting, and this Station is Named after the fact that this station is located at a place where two rivers meet.[3]

History[]

  • August 10 2017: This station completed construction.[4]
  • August 11 2017: This station began services.
  • March 13 2018: Exit D is added to this station to connect to the Haisan Railway Station of the Same Name.[5]

Fun Facts[]

  • Prior to the reconstruction of this Station, it was a Ground Station and had 6 Platforms, 2 of which reserved for Line 2003 and 2 of which reserved for Line 2004. However, following the reconstruction of this Station, the number of platforms had been reduced to 4, and it is already known that the 2 new reserved platforms are constructed for Line 2003, and spoilers for the planned route of Line 2003 are also seen near the reserved tracks for said line. The fate of Line 2004 is now unknown.

Fun Facts[]

  • This station has been jokingly referred to as a "Matcha Roll Cake".[3]
  • The color scheme of this station alludes to Creepers in Minecraft as per the request of the island owner. As a result, a creeper station art is seen at two ends of the platform, with creeper heads featured at the station pillars and the corridors.[4]
  • This station features the first and currently the only set of Unisex Toilets in Nazca Railway, with lavatories being featured at the passageway as well.
  • This station shares structure and exit numbers with Kirameki Electric Railway Citybranch Line Rollhill Island Station.

History[]

  • May 7 2019: This Station completed construction.
  • May 8 2019: This Station began services.
  • August 15 2021: This station completed exit naming.[5]
  • May 23 2022: Exit F is added to this station to connect to the Kirameki Electric Railway Station of the Same Name.[6]

Fun Facts[]

  • This Station is the first Ground Station to be built on Pegasus Line.[3][4]
  • To reduce the space required for Pegasus Line to climb from the Underground Section to the Elevated Section, this station adopts side platforms.[5]
  • This Station is named after the fact that there is an abundance of Poppies near this station. As Roses do not exist in Minecraft, and Poppies in Minecraft resemble Roses in real life, they are used as a substitution for roses in this station.[6]
  • The design of this station takes references from Cyan Loop Station prior to its Phoenix Line expansion, as well as Blackstone Village Station and Lower Shack Station.
  • The Chinese Name of this Station is slightly modified to its current name as the direct translation of its English Name would be too long and unspecific, and using the Direct Chinese Translation of Roses would cause ambiguity with the Airport Core Programme in Hong Kong, which at the time was commonly called the Rose Garden Project.[7]

History[]

  • November 20 2022: This station completed construction.[8] At the same day, this station began services.

Fun Facts[]

  • This Station shares Chinese Names with Lockin Station of Arcgo City Railway. However, while this station is located in Rover, Lockin Station is located in Torrent.
  • Due to Historical Reasons, This Station is the last station to feature "Station Icons" until the reinstatement of "Station Icons" during the Station Title and Icon Upgrade Scheme of Thin River Station in Season 4, Episode 5.
  • The builder of Nazca Railway came up with the name of this station, which is derived from its original biome.[2] The Gold Color Scheme of this station is also used to symbolize plentiful fields.[3]

History[]

  • January 10 2025: This Station began construction.
  • January 12 2025: This Station completed construction.[4]
  • January 13 2025: This Station began services. Rover Line extends from Rover Stadium Station to Upper Rover Station through this station.

Rougewood Station is a station on Starshore Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Prymea. Passengers may also use this station to change to SLT Line 2601, Line 2611 (Rougewood Stop).

Fun Facts[]

  • While this Station is situated at the border of the Cometsilk and Prymea Districts, most of the station structure lays within the latter.
  • The Chinese Name of this Station alludes to Natsuki Rin in Yes! Pretty Cure 5 of the Pretty Cure Franchise, while the English Name of this Station is an Amalgamation of the words Rouge, which refers to the Color Red in French and is in turn used to allude to Fire and Flames for the Character motif, and Wood; Overall, it's a translation of the character's name "Natsuki", which means "Summer Tree".

History[]

  • April 24 2026: This Station began construction.
  • April 25 2026: This Station completed construction.
  • April 26 2026: Starshore Line extends from Nail Bight Checkpoint to Welliant Plateau Station through this station. Starshore Line is established.

Station Title and Soundtrack[]

  • The Station Title of this Station is Dionysian Amphitheater.
  • This Station features two soundtracks that belong to the album "Of Soil and Splendor, Of Jest and Joy".
Name of the Soundtrack Length (mm:ss)
Dionysian Amphitheater 01:35
Chant of the Sacred Vessel 01:02

Fun Facts[]

  • While this Station is an Underground Station, the design of this station is similar to that of a Pseudoground Station.
  • The Station Pillars of this station makes use of arch designs, and is much more sparse than average stations. Also, a transparent enclosed space appeared beneath the platforms so that the pillars can "mirror" each other. Enclosed Spaces are also seen behind the tracks, and Station Signs are placed above the tracks to compensate for the lower number of station signs due to sparse pillars.
  • A Colosseum is built outside Exit A1 of this station.

History[]

  • May 13 2022: The Concourse and Platforms of this station completed construction.[2]
  • May 14 2022: The Colosseum of this station completed construction.[3] At the same day, this station began services.
  • April 9 2023: The Station Title Banner of this station is added.
  • February 3 2025: This station completed its Station Title and Icon Upgrade Scheme.[4]
  • July 17 2025: The Station Icon of this station is added.

History[]

The initial route of Route 10 extends from the two north-south oriented roads at Prosand Station as a northeastern bypass of Los Sengas. This route enables drivers to travel between sub-urban areas of Los Sengas Continent without passing through its center. As this route radiated from Prosand, a large detour is made within Prosand at the time of this Route's construction, causing the route length to exceed 43 km.

When Route 10 began services, there were only 4 exits, namely at Circle Pit, Prosand, Stardust Road and Spinstone Plane, and was also the first Route to feature a non-expressway section. Along the route, the Junction between Warsaw Road and Marisa Road featured traffic lights, and due to sparse development, traffic was also very low. Hence, buses also avoided this route. However, before 2020, this route was the only external access to and from Intus Orient Village, causing vehicles to and from Intus Orient to pass through Cometsilk central very frequently and bottlenecks were formed.

However, as development at Los Sengas east began, Prosand, Egress, Comrel Island, Peacean Island and Clouds saw significant development, and Route 10 became a main artery at the east of Los Sengas, seeing an increasing traffic flow by the day. Vehicles to and from Intus Orient could now make use of Route 2 as well. Under these circumstances, the detour at Prosand became a problem for drivers who wanted to travel between Rover, Ingress, Egress and Torrent as it increased the travel time significantly without any alternatives provided. Moreover, regardless of the route taken, passing through Prosand was mandatory for drivers, further increasing traffic loads at the Warsaw Road, Ning Yat Road, Marisa Road Junction.

As a result, the re-routing works for Route 10 was proposed in 2021, with the new section extending to the south from east Diamond Sand, forming a junction with Route 2 at the east of Calmé, before joining the original Route 10 between Gentle Island and Waterbelt Garden. The works began in April 2022 and has since been completed. Currently, passengers between Clouds and Egress no longer had to pass through Prosand, and the section at Marisa Road is no longer a part of Route 10, significantly shortening the length of Route 10 from 43 km to 32 km.

Chronological Order[]

  • January 13 2018: Route 10 began construction.
  • January 14 2018: Section between Intus Orient and Prosand completed construction.
  • January 15 2018: Section between Prosand and Flamelute Island completed construction.
  • January 16 2018: Section between Flamelute Island and Glacier completed construction.
  • January 17 2018: Section between Glacier and Upper Rover completed construction. Route 10 completed construction.
  • April 5 2022: Route 10 rerouting works began construction.
  • January 26 2025: This route becomes connected with Route 3.

Fun Facts[]

  • At the time of its completion, this route was 43.07 km long, and is still the longest Route in Los Sengas to date.
  • This route is the quickest route to complete construction, with the route completing construction just 4 days after construction began.
  • The Sheung Yuen Bridge along this route is the longest suspension bridge in Los Sengas at 4000 m long.
  • This Route wass the first Route in Los Sengas to feature a non-expressway section, with Marisa Road featuring Traffic Lights. However, after the latest re-route, this is no longer the case.
  • All sections of this Route have their independent road names, a rare instance among Routes in Los Sengas.

Existing Section[]

Dansein Road[]

This is a 6 to 11 lane road serves as the trunk road through Dansein and Northern Dansein. The road currently spans 3.8km, spurring from Route 12 to North Coast Road.

Planned Sections[]

Tin Tak Street[]

This 6 to 8 lane road is planned to be the first expressway in Los Sengas named as a street.

Airport Connector[]

This 6 lane road is planned to be the access to the airport parking, drop-off and pick-up areas, etc.. It would also provide as a backup access to the maintenance area.

Route 15, formerly known as Oasis Bay Highway, is one of the Routes in Los Sengas. It runs between Twenty-Second Continent and Borealis. It is projected to extend to the east in the future.

Contents

  • 1 Sections
  • 2 Districts Served
  • 3 Fun Facts
  • 4 Gallery
  • 5 Citations and References

Sections[]

  • Strait of Freedom
  • Oldon Town
  • Abysmal Bay Tunnel
  • Snipe Valley
  • Suez
  • Mount Spadrago

Districts Served[]

  • Twenty-Second Continent
  • Jupiter
  • Oasis Bay
  • Prymea
  • Borealis

Fun Facts[]

  • The highway itself is also named Oasis Bay Motorway and Borealis Highway in different parts respectively, in which the former part was also the original name before this highway was arranged a Route number.
  • The area served by Route 15, Oasis Bay Line and Snow White Line are overall similar; This is due to Route 15 being designed to travel along the south of Oasis Bay Line inside Jupiter and Oasis Bay initially, and Oasis Bay Line was later planned to reversely follow along Route 15 inside Prymea and Borealis; Whereas Snow White Line was overall planned to travel along Route 15 as well.
    • The situation also caused Oasis Bay Line to have partial section of its tracks situated right below Route 15 (Parrot Mount to Lake Yore, excluding Mount Qin West and Spring Point), similar to Luxter Line at Coast Edge and Thick River.

Fun Facts[]

  • The West Metropolis Archipelago Section of this Route is built in Four Phases as follows:
    • Phase 1: Route 15A - Route 8
    • Phase 2: Route 8 - Route 5
    • Phase 3: Route 12 - Route 9B
    • Phase 4: Route 5 - Route 12
  • The Odyssey and Jupiter Section of this Route formerly belonged to Route 9B and Route 15A respectively. However, after the completion of Phase 4, these Sections became a Part of this Route.
  • This Route does NOT provide direct access with Route 7 and Route 9 despite passing under them; However, as this Route do provide access with Route 9B and Route 9C which are both parts of the Route 9 network, this Route still does interchange with Route 9 indirectly.

Route 2 is one of the initially planned Routes in Los Sengas. It is designed to provide transport services for Los Sengas Continent, and had extended to Cometsilk and Clouds on April 2018. Currently, it is 19.131 km long.

Contents

  • 1 Districts Served
  • 2 Road Sections
  • 3 History
  • 4 Fun Facts

  • 6 Citations and References

Districts Served[]

  • Sava
  • Downtown
  • Katadelphia
  • Flask
  • Yowah
  • Cometsilk
  • Clouds

Road Sections[]

  • Twelve of June Bridge

History[]

  • April 2015: Plans for this route are in place.
  • May 8 2015: Metropolis JCT, Po Fong Exit completed construction.
  • June-July 2015: Metro Spring Exit, Katadelphia Section completed construction.
  • August-September 2015: Threeler Exit completed construction.
  • October 2015: Sava Section completed construction.
  • November 2015: Flask West, Flask East Exits completed construction.
  • December 30 2015: Grass Crack Exit completed construction.
  • December 31 2015: Sava-Yowah section began services.
  • 2016: Bonyal JCT, Southend Exit completed construction.
  • April 2018: Weaving Plate Exit, Twelve of June Bridge completed construction.
  • March 2022: Route 2 extended to Clouds.
  • January 23 2023: High Approach Road South Exit completed construction.

Fun Facts[]

  • Despite being the second route to be planned, Route 2 is the first route in Los Sengas to be constructed.
  • The Metropolis JCT has been subject to multiple re-constructions.
  • Bonyal and Southend Exits are only constructed later on.
  • The west end of this Route connects directly to Route 3.
  • Exit 4 is re-constructed due to Sava Line construction.
  • San Annis Station of Arcgo Line shares structure with this route.
  • Parts of Bravo Line shares structure with this route (Between Metropolis and Flask East)
  • Flask East exit is the first loop exit in Los Sengas.
  • This Route passes through both terminals of Mayler Airport.

Route 5 is one of the Routes in Los Sengas. It runs between Downtown and Xofa, connecting with West Metropolis Archipelago and Peckern in the process. Plans are also in place for this route to extend to Festival.

Contents

  • 1 Districts Served
  • 2 Development Trivia

  • 6 Citations and References

Districts Served[]

  • Downtown
  • West Metropolis Archipelago
    • Hatace Island
    • Sanfo Island
    • Middle Island
      • Rollhill Island (Through Rollhill-Middle Island Tunnel)
    • Anshield Island
    • Info Island
    • Bulldoze Island (Under Construction)
  • Peckern
    • Milead Pond
  • Xofa (Through Xofa Highway)

Development Trivia[]

Original Plans of Route[]

Before the official construction of this route, the suggested proposals of this route are as follows:[3]

  1. North Route: This route branches off from Route 2 near Jayler Road, and passes through Ponsand Island, Ponrest Island and Belt Island before approaching Peckern near Gull Woods, with no exits set up along the route. This route is represented by the red line at the picture below, and later became the route for Delta Line at West Metropolis Archipelago.
  2. Central Route: This route branches off from Route 4 near Lean Forest Island, and passes under Middle Island, Info Island and Bulldoze Island before landing near Peckern Forest, with exits added upon request of island owners. This route is represented by the yellow line at the picture below. Ultimately, this route was chosen after a few modifications were made to it. Instaed of landing at Lean Forest Island, the current Route 5 involves passing through Hatace Island and Seat River, with the Peckern end being located at Milead Pond.
  3. South Route: This route also branches off from Route 4 near Miner Bay Depot. However, instead of going to Peckern, it goes to Twenty-Second Continent after passing through Shony Island and Tenbal Island using tunnels and bridges, before passing through Airship Island to reach Peckern. It is represented by the orange color at the picture below, and later became the route for Route 7.
  4. Car Ferry Proposal: This route involves using a train that carries cars, and reaches Peckern Continent using a newly built railway tunnel. While detailed plans for this proposal never surface, it is implied that Fox Line travels in a similar route to what this proposal could have used.

Fun Facts[]

  • Exit 9 of this Route provides connections with Cities Transit Route 5 Station.

History[]

  • January 12 2016: Plans for this route are in place.
  • March 24 2016: Seat River JCT Phase I completed construction. Hatace Island Exit began services.
  • 2016: Sanfo Island exit began services.
  • 2016: Middle Island exit began services.
  • May 16 2016: Milead Pond exit began services.
  • June 2 2016: Hatace Island exit completed upgrades.
  • June 12 2016: Anshield Island exit began services.
  • 2016: Seat River JCT Phase II completed construction, connecting to Route 4.
  • August 30 2016: Info Island exit began services.
  • August 30 2016: Intus Occident Gateway completed construction.
  • September 14 2016: Intus Occident exit began services.
  • October 22 2016: New Judy Island exit added to Route 5 after repeated requests from the island owner.
  • April 10 2022: Xofa Highway exit began services.

In Fact, the predecessor of Route 5 Station is this station, as this station also used the structure that Route 5 Station currently uses.

Route 7 is one of the Routes in Los Sengas. It runs between TriPaw and Xofa, connecting with West Metropolis Archipelago, Twenty-Second Continent and Peckern in the process.

Development Trivia[]

This route originally passes through Python, but as Kallen Road has alread replaced the section of Route 7 that runs along Python, this route has now detoured to the north and merges with the original plans of Route 8 and heads for Peckern Continent.

Original Plans of Route[]

There were many proposals of the route for Route 7, and they are listed as follows;

  • Airship Island, Blu Trove Bay Route:
    • This route involves Route 7 turning to the east and setting up an exit at Airship Island before landing at Blu Trove Bay of the Peckern Continent after passing through the Comp Ward JCT.
  • Airship Island, Wood Wound Route:
    • This route involves Route 7 going to Airship Island using a bridge and connecting to Wood Wound Road at Peckern Continent afte rpassing through the Comp Ward JCT. However, the setting up of the exit at Airship Island would be dependent on developmental needs.
  • Branch Proposal:
    • This proposal skips Airship Island and goes directly to Peckern Continent, connecting with Peckern Viaduct and setting up exits at Milead Pond and Wood Wound in the process. While this proposal was ultimately adopted, Route 7 was instead connected directly to Peckern Coast Bridge Road and intersects with Peckern East Coast Road to save construction costs. However, this proposal was highly dependent on transportation connections around Milead POnd, and connection works are done around Milead Pond during construction works.

Afterwards, Pekcern developers began reconstructing the above proposals and caused Route 7 to land on Airship Island on June 2022, before connecting to Dufol along the mountains of the south coast for preliminary works of Dufol Transport. The Peckern Section of Route 7 is subsequently named "Greater Development Predicament Expressway".

Subsequent Development[]

Suggestions have been made to extend Route 7 to Xofa in order to enhance connectivity. This proposal from Twenty-Second Continent was approved by developers from Peckern, but it was delayed to July 2022 due to difficulties at the Peckern section.

History[]

  • September 15 2016: Route 7 began construction.
  • September 16 2016: Nick Fin Bridge completed construction.
  • September 18 2016: Diamond Pool Bridge completed construction.
  • January 3 2020: Diamond Pool North JCT completed construction.
  • January 9 2020: Zerda Hill Exit, Java Beach Exit completed construction.
  • January 11 2020: Comp Ward Exit completed construction.
  • January 12 2020: Milead Pond JCT, Wood Wound Exit completed construction.
  • February 2 2020: Halozy Exit completed construction.
  • June 20 2021: Xofa Bypass completed construction.
  • April 2 2022: Halozy Exit completed reconstruction.
  • July 21 2022: Peckern Section completed reconstruction.

Future Development[]

When Route 7 began planning development at Nagasora, a branch at Darey Terrace was built to Nagasora to reduce traffic flow at Kallen Road. However, this plan was replaced by a new road (Serendipity Drive) connecting Routes 7 and 8, and Route 8 is instead used for Trunk Road Traffic to and from Nagasora.
